Elections | The Underdogs

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot?

Unique Selling Point:
Independent candidates are a new addition to South Africa's democracy. What does an independent candidates election campaign look like - is it enough and IF they secure the seat they dream of - will IT be enough to make the level of impact this country needs?

Summary:
Premise:
Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot?

There are 325 political parties who will be taking part in this year’s elections.

But standing outside the confines of a long-held electoral party system are the outliers:
11 independent candidates who are going against the grain -who believe they can make a difference with only one seat.

https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/political-parties-independent-candidates-sign-code-conduct

Why?

Voters are desperate for alternatives and some people online have been pushing the independent candidate option as a viable one - but is it?

In order to answer this question, we spoke to several independent candidates to establish how they will go about instituting impactful changes. Repeatedly, all except one - Anele Mda - stated they are limited as they only have one seat. Begging the question, why pursue independent candidacy if one already feels limited and powerless.

In addition, as they are all championing varying issues it provides an opportunity to debate some of the key voter concerns.




Further information:
Interviews

Anele Mda

She was introduced to politics by her father who was a dedicated member of the ANC. A former COPE MP, Anele had her share of controversy during her tenure. For instance, in 2009, she was suspended from COPE for making sexist and racist remarks. She is an extremely head strong and fiery individual who seems very convicted in her beliefs.
Her political experience makes her the strongest of the independent candidates.
Controversy seems to follow her as her reaction to the absence of independent candidate photographs raied a few eyebrows. However, when one understand the IEC hasn’t even updated its website to reflect the existence of independent candidates - then perhaps one can comprehend the frustrations.
Anele’s key focus areas:-
Unemployment - she says she will actively challenge the 12 month internship period because companies are compensated for employing interns yet they fail to make meaningful change. She says it should be a 3 year internship as most entry level roles require 3 years experience. I asked if the issue wasn't sufficient employment opportunities for all coupled with limited entrepreneurial pursuits. In addition, given the climate - would a mandatory three year internship not result in locking new graduates out of an already scarce job market. I also highlighted that the government has spent billions of Rands on youth employment programmes, yet unemployment keeps rising.
Scrapping the tender system - she says it has only benefitted a few and needs to go


Tshepo Mogano

Was formerly in the SANDF for eight years, he said he left because the army did not meet up with his expectations as it was being run unprofessionally. He then worked for a PPP specialising in facilities management, where he was a PA to the CEO he says he is very active in his community in Pretoria and established the body corporate at the estate where he purchased property.

He managed to buy the property after he left the PPP and went into the tender business. It would be interesting to juxtapose his views on tenders versus Anele’s intention to have the system scrapped.

He has championed a number of small projects in his area and intends to replicate these at provincial level. When asked about policy implementation he stated he will learn as he goes along - it seems he hasn't conducted research in order to understand the political climate in which he intends to operate . Again , he repeatedly referenced the fact he would only have one seat as a barrier to impact he had no how-to-strategy regarding the policies he intends to further. For example , he made reference to drug rehabilitation centres but he did not know about the budgets of the status quo rehabilitation centres around the province. He was uncertain when I asked if he would vote with the ANC and if he would ever receive it in exchange for his vote .
Tshepo had a particularly terrible interview at Newzroom Afrika last week where he stated he would vote with the ANC and that Panyaza Lesufi is doing a great job as premier.

Political Analyst:

Otsile Nkadimeng

Highly articulate 19 year old who will be voting for the first time this year.
Otsile Nkadimeng is the Founder and Executive Director of So We Vote, a Youth Voting Advocacy Group. He is also the lead organiser of Fridays for Future South Africa and the co-founder of the Sundial Movement, a Climate Network that connects high school students to take collective action on Climate Change. Alongside his role as a Climate Activist.

Press Release:


Going At It Alone

With just days to go before the national elections and a buffet of options, South Africans are facing tough choices. On paper, political parties will come head-to-head with the newly minted independent candidates on two of the three ballot papers, a conundrum that voters have never encountered before. But short on a strong traditional supporter base and the resources for a competitive election campaign, do independent candidates have a real chance to make an impact in these elections. In the battle between political parties and independent candidates, Carte Blanche examines who’s got the upper hand?

Producer: Harri Vithi | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


The Underdogs
Viz: Different political parties campaigns –from facebook…Harri will include links
VO 1: It’s election season and parties are splurging on campaigns - hiring stadia, music
artists and throwing t-shirts. But this year, South Africans are faced with a completely
different choice on the ballot paper: vote for a political party OR take a chance on an
independent candidate.
Viz: Johannesburg skyline, traffic and then Masa in the vehicle
LINK: CLIP C0072 @00:38
It’s early morning here in Johannesburg and we’re making our way to a manifesto launch
at Constitution Hill but this will be a different kind of manifesto launch - it’s that of an
independent candidate
Viz:C0026…C0027..
VO 2: Independent candidates aren’t associated with political parties and for the first
time they’re being allowed to contest national and provincial elections.
Viz: Let’s use the social media montage Stenette created here
VO 3: In a landmark ruling in 2020, the constitutional court said limiting representation in
the national and provincial legislatures to candidates from political parties only was
unconstitutional.
Last April, the signing of the Electoral Amendment Bill paved the way for independent
candidates to contest elections.
Viz: montage then split screen of hero shots of Anele and Tshepo
VO 4: There are 11 independent candidates contesting this month’s elections. We’re on
the campaign trail with two of these political hopefuls.
Viz: hero shot of Anele
One with a proven political background…
UPSOUND ANELE - under viz of hero shot
Viz: hero shot of Tshepo
CLIP0017 00:09:14:18 - 00:09:46:17 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate

… There's value and there's power in being an underdog— I'm a big dog in the political
landscape.
…the other a novice in the world of politics.
NOTE: This is Tshepo’s sit down interview in the garden
@ 00:37:13:24 - 00:37:44:14 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate -
Dynamite really does come in small packages - I'm going to give them a problem in Parliament.
Viz: general of Consitution Hill
VO 5: We meet Anele Mda at the Women's Jail on Constitutional Hill. As a former member
of the ANC and COPE - she’s no stranger to the cut and thrust of party politics
UPSOUND MASA, Cam A, C0102

@ 01:58 Masa
…you're coming in as an independent - there is no party backing you are the nerves a little
different
@ 02:15 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate
…at the core of my nerves is the overwhelming desire and recommitment to not fail the people
of South Africa.
Masa: I will be in the audience eagerly listening as well!
Anele takes a deep breath
VO 6: A manifesto sets out a party or candidate’s policies, and support for Mda’s
campaign rides on how it’s received.
Visual sequence: C0138, C0139, C0140 - Anele walkies with manifesto in hand
VO 7: In some ways, independents get to play by their own rules.
Viz: Masa and Tshepo walking in estate
VO 8: Pretoria-based Tshepo Mogano is a busy man: he’s the chairperson of his body
corporate, the section leader of the CPF, and a businessman.
@ 00:22:27:18 - 00:22:30:13 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
I don’t have a manifesto. I don't have to have a manifesto.

@ 00:22:31:05 - 00:22:32:11 Masa
Wait! You don't have a manifesto!?
Tshepo: Yes.
Masa: How do you then go and sell what you are proposing without a manifesto?
@ 00:29:20:18 - 00:29:30:00 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
… Masa, manifestos are a lie. And I want to tell South Africans today what manifestos are.
Manifestos are love letters that never materialized into relationships.
00:29:31:15 - 00:30:02:24 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
—I'm telling South Africans there is a new kid on the block called an independent candidate —-
I'm going to do very well because I'm one with the people. I'm not the guy that doesn't know how
much bread costs.
UPSOUND OTSILE NKADEMENG
@ 06:52 Otsile Nkadimeng, So We Vote
I think that a manifesto is critical in a democracy - especially like ours - where we’ve seen
promises where a promise is not kept.
VO 9: Otsile Nkadimeng is the executive director and co-founder of So We Vote – an
organization focused on voter education.
@ 06:52 Otsile Nkadimeng, So We Vote
It gives us a point of reference 5 years from now when we vote again to say Tshepo promised
us xyz you didn't deliver so we got rid of you.
Viz: Anele walking to launch room with manifesto in hand …Anele sitting upfront with cameras
set up in room…Masa watching and taking notes
UPSOUND ANELE MDA MANIFESTO SPEECH
I am committed to making a change in South Africa…
Viz options of Masa listening to manifesto: C0118/C0119/C0121/C0122 (Masa paging through
manifesto). C0123 - Anele speaking - Masa silhouetted while she speaks)
C0171
00:26

So there you have it, that's what you get when you run as an independent. A midweek
manifesto in a small venue. They don't have the luxury and the resources that the
political parties who are well established do who are bussing supporters in, feeding them
and giving them party t-shirts. It does seem the independent candidates are starting off
on a backfoot
VO 10: While Mda’s manifesto was broadcast nationally, Mogano pounds the streets,
going door-to-door in Pretoria’s suburbs.
His is a humble operation when compared to the multi-million Rand campaigns of the
country’s bigger parties.
UPSOUND TSHEPO MOGANO, CAM 3, CLIP C0036
CAM 3, CLIP C0036@ 0:08 Speaking Sesotho
Knock-knock, knock-knock!. How are you? Please may I speak with you by the gate?…
…opens the gate slightly…Hello! How are you, my brother?..shakes hands
VO 11: Mogano became an independent candidate by accident.
While the IEC needs at least 1000 nominations for an independent to be registered,
Mogano’s community stepped up and secured 50,000 signatures on his behalf,
propelling him into the political arena.
Viz of Theresapark before cutting to the interview
CARD 3
C0018
@00:23 Masa
You've been campaigning on the streets, how do people generally receive you?
@ 00:26 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
People are shocked, I mean people don't even know what an independent candidate is...I mean
they think an independent candidate is a political party
VO 12: Apart from a focused strategy, success in politics takes big money. Both Mda and
Mogano have been relying on donations and dipping into their savings.

Viz:
https://www.tiktok.com/@anelemda/video/7368012734731980038?is_from_webapp=1&sender_
device=pc
Viz option: C0016

VO 13: According to our Mda and Mogano, people with cash and vested interests are
maneuvering behind the scenes offering independents campaign money in exchange for
support on specific policies.
Viz: C0016 - Anele looking at phone while seated in hall
CARD 3- C0018/ CARD 2 CLIP @01:47 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
..I'm going to give you X amount of money but when you get to parliament xyz you don't talk
about it ...issue of land you don't talk about, the issue of borders you don't talk about…
CLIP C0018 & C0151 @ 08:24 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate
I had a dubious suspicious offer of some millions 3 weeks ago—and I had to walk away.
VO 14: It would have been a long-shot investment on a candidate not even guaranteed a
seat. Assuming they get the required number of votes – no matter how many they
eventually accumulate – independents can only get one seat. Which begs the question:
why would anyone invest in their campaigns?
VO 15: The answer lies in the assumption that no single party will secure a majority –
either at national level or in some of the Provinces. And it’s here that independents
become important.
UPSOUND ANELE MDA
@ 00:08:16:03 - 00:08:49:01 Anele Mda, Independent Candidates
— at this point in time, the emergence of independent candidates threatens and rattles the
status quo, both from the part of political parties that are opposition, but also on the governing
party as well.
@ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidates
It looks like we are going to be the actual kingmakers.
VO 16: Through their seat - independents may have the power to swing votes in favour of
particular political decisions.
Hence, the term “kingmaker”
VO 17: Mda isn’t a fan of the concept.
CLIP 00017 @ 00:06:29:15 - 00:07:14:04 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate
.. I'm not going to Parliament to be an addition of numerical strength to any political party.
UPSOUND ANELE MDA
CLIP 0017 @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate

I'm not looking to be a kingmaker because I'm saying the throne is empty and I'm gunning for
the throne.
CLIP 0017 @00:16:59:12 - 00:17:01:12 Masa: So that's first prize presidency?
Anele Mda: Absolutely. The first prize is the presidency.
VO 18: Mda’s ambition is impressive, but the likelihood of an independent becoming
president is extremely small. So, with just one seat available to them, are they a viable
option for voters?
@ 01:53 Masa : As a first time voter would you consider voting for an independent
@ 02:20 Otsile Nkadimeng, So we Vote
I would consider voting for an independent should the right kind of independent emerge. I want
a leader or representative I can trust. Currently my dilemma with the party system is I have lots
of parties to choose from but the people who are running under these parties can I trust them?
@ 03:22 Otsile Nkadimeng, So we Vote
I recognize the imperfections of SA democracy at this present time. @ 07:40 Otsile Nkadimeng,
So we Vote
… so it would be a trade off do you choose the party because we trust a few individuals but it
comes with a few rotten apples or would you rather go for an independent who you can more
directly hire and fire
VO 19: Now, for many of the independent candidates, it’s about sparking change in an
imperfect system.
DAY 2, CARD 3, C0006 @ 03:57 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
… I've sent an appointment —- as a member of the provincial legislature on the 30th of May so
the appointment is already set so it's just for me to go honour it.
VO 20: So confident is Mogano about his chances, he’s booked his appointment with
Parliament just as the counting of votes begins. It’s an impressive level of confidence
that belies the uphill battle faced by the independent candidates contesting next week’s
elections. Some are bigger names than others and stand a better chance of being in the
final Parliamentary mix.
VO 21: If they make it, the question then becomes whether their voices will be heard in an
increasingly combative National Assembly.”
—-----THE END —---

PROMOS
Promo 1
VO 1: Short on supporters and resources, independent candidates are the new kids on
the ballot paper
00:29:31:15 - 00:30:02:24 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
—Today, I'm telling South Africans there is a new kid on the block called an independent
candidate —-
CLIP 0017 @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate
I'm not looking to be a kingmaker because I'm saying the throne is empty and I'm gunning for
the throne.
VO 2: A potential game changer on the ballot
—---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Promo 2
VO 3: The manifestos have been delivered… the posters are up… and the clock is ticking
down to election day…
UPSOUND ANELE MDA
@ 00:08:16:03 - 00:08:49:01 Anele Mda, Independent Candidates
— at this point in time, the emergence of independent candidates threatens and rattles the
status quo
VO 4: But in the battle between political parties and independent candidates, who’s got
the upper hand?
…………………………………………………………………………………………………………..
Promo 3
VO 5: Independent candidates are the new kid on the ballot paper.
00:29:31:15 - 00:30:02:24 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate
—there is a new kid on the block called an independent candidate —- I'm not the guy that
doesn't know how much bread costs.

VO 6: But could they be a real game changer in the upcoming elections?
CLIP 0017 @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate
I'm saying the throne is empty and I'm gunning for the throne.
CLIP 0017 @00:16:59:12 - 00:17:01:12 Masa: So that's first prize presidency?
Anele Mda: Absolutely. The first prize is the presidency.

But this year, South Africans are faced with a completely different choice on the ballot paper: vote for a political party OR take a chance on an independent candidate. Viz: Johannesburg skyline, traffic and then Masa in the vehicle LINK: CLIP C0072 @00:38 It’s early morning here in Johannesburg and we’re making our way to a manifesto launch at Constitution Hill but this will be a different kind of manifesto launch - it’s that of an independent candidate Viz:C0026…C0027.. VO 2: Independent candidates aren’t associated with political parties and for the first time they’re being allowed to contest national and provincial elections. Viz: Let’s use the social media montage Stenette created here VO 3: In a landmark ruling in 2020, the constitutional court said limiting representation in the national and provincial legislatures to candidates from political parties only was unconstitutional. Last April, the signing of the Electoral Amendment Bill paved the way for independent candidates to contest elections. Viz: montage then split screen of hero shots of Anele and Tshepo VO 4: There are 11 independent candidates contesting this month’s elections. We’re on the campaign trail with two of these political hopefuls. Viz: hero shot of Anele One with a proven political background… UPSOUND ANELE - under viz of hero shot Viz: hero shot of Tshepo CLIP0017 00:09:14:18 - 00:09:46:17 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate … There's value and there's power in being an underdog— I'm a big dog in the political landscape. …the other a novice in the world of politics. NOTE: This is Tshepo’s sit down interview in the garden @ 00:37:13:24 - 00:37:44:14 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate - Dynamite really does come in small packages - I'm going to give them a problem in Parliament. Viz: general of Consitution Hill VO 5: We meet Anele Mda at the Women's Jail on Constitutional Hill. As a former member of the ANC and COPE - she’s no stranger to the cut and thrust of party politics UPSOUND MASA, Cam A, C0102 @ 01:58 Masa …you're coming in as an independent - there is no party backing you are the nerves a little different @ 02:15 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate …at the core of my nerves is the overwhelming desire and recommitment to not fail the people of South Africa. Masa: I will be in the audience eagerly listening as well! Anele takes a deep breath VO 6: A manifesto sets out a party or candidate’s policies, and support for Mda’s campaign rides on how it’s received. Visual sequence: C0138, C0139, C0140 - Anele walkies with manifesto in hand VO 7: In some ways, independents get to play by their own rules. Viz: Masa and Tshepo walking in estate VO 8: Pretoria-based Tshepo Mogano is a busy man: he’s the chairperson of his body corporate, the section leader of the CPF, and a businessman. @ 00:22:27:18 - 00:22:30:13 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate I don’t have a manifesto. I don't have to have a manifesto. @ 00:22:31:05 - 00:22:32:11 Masa Wait! You don't have a manifesto!? Tshepo: Yes. Masa: How do you then go and sell what you are proposing without a manifesto? @ 00:29:20:18 - 00:29:30:00 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate … Masa, manifestos are a lie. And I want to tell South Africans today what manifestos are. Manifestos are love letters that never materialized into relationships. 00:29:31:15 - 00:30:02:24 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate —I'm telling South Africans there is a new kid on the block called an independent candidate —- I'm going to do very well because I'm one with the people. I'm not the guy that doesn't know how much bread costs. UPSOUND OTSILE NKADEMENG @ 06:52 Otsile Nkadimeng, So We Vote I think that a manifesto is critical in a democracy - especially like ours - where we’ve seen promises where a promise is not kept. VO 9: Otsile Nkadimeng is the executive director and co-founder of So We Vote – an organization focused on voter education. @ 06:52 Otsile Nkadimeng, So We Vote It gives us a point of reference 5 years from now when we vote again to say Tshepo promised us xyz you didn't deliver so we got rid of you. Viz: Anele walking to launch room with manifesto in hand …Anele sitting upfront with cameras set up in room…Masa watching and taking notes UPSOUND ANELE MDA MANIFESTO SPEECH I am committed to making a change in South Africa… Viz options of Masa listening to manifesto: C0118/C0119/C0121/C0122 (Masa paging through manifesto). C0123 - Anele speaking - Masa silhouetted while she speaks) C0171 00:26 So there you have it, that's what you get when you run as an independent. A midweek manifesto in a small venue. They don't have the luxury and the resources that the political parties who are well established do who are bussing supporters in, feeding them and giving them party t-shirts. It does seem the independent candidates are starting off on a backfoot VO 10: While Mda’s manifesto was broadcast nationally, Mogano pounds the streets, going door-to-door in Pretoria’s suburbs. His is a humble operation when compared to the multi-million Rand campaigns of the country’s bigger parties. UPSOUND TSHEPO MOGANO, CAM 3, CLIP C0036 CAM 3, CLIP C0036@ 0:08 Speaking Sesotho Knock-knock, knock-knock!. How are you? Please may I speak with you by the gate?… …opens the gate slightly…Hello! How are you, my brother?..shakes hands VO 11: Mogano became an independent candidate by accident. While the IEC needs at least 1000 nominations for an independent to be registered, Mogano’s community stepped up and secured 50,000 signatures on his behalf, propelling him into the political arena. Viz of Theresapark before cutting to the interview CARD 3 C0018 @00:23 Masa You've been campaigning on the streets, how do people generally receive you? @ 00:26 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate People are shocked, I mean people don't even know what an independent candidate is...I mean they think an independent candidate is a political party VO 12: Apart from a focused strategy, success in politics takes big money. Both Mda and Mogano have been relying on donations and dipping into their savings. Viz: https://www.tiktok.com/@anelemda/video/7368012734731980038?is_from_webapp=1&sender_ device=pc Viz option: C0016 VO 13: According to our Mda and Mogano, people with cash and vested interests are maneuvering behind the scenes offering independents campaign money in exchange for support on specific policies. Viz: C0016 - Anele looking at phone while seated in hall CARD 3- C0018/ CARD 2 CLIP @01:47 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate ..I'm going to give you X amount of money but when you get to parliament xyz you don't talk about it ...issue of land you don't talk about, the issue of borders you don't talk about… CLIP C0018 & C0151 @ 08:24 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate I had a dubious suspicious offer of some millions 3 weeks ago—and I had to walk away. VO 14: It would have been a long-shot investment on a candidate not even guaranteed a seat. Assuming they get the required number of votes – no matter how many they eventually accumulate – independents can only get one seat. Which begs the question: why would anyone invest in their campaigns? VO 15: The answer lies in the assumption that no single party will secure a majority – either at national level or in some of the Provinces. And it’s here that independents become important. UPSOUND ANELE MDA @ 00:08:16:03 - 00:08:49:01 Anele Mda, Independent Candidates — at this point in time, the emergence of independent candidates threatens and rattles the status quo, both from the part of political parties that are opposition, but also on the governing party as well. @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidates It looks like we are going to be the actual kingmakers. VO 16: Through their seat - independents may have the power to swing votes in favour of particular political decisions. Hence, the term “kingmaker” VO 17: Mda isn’t a fan of the concept. CLIP 00017 @ 00:06:29:15 - 00:07:14:04 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate .. I'm not going to Parliament to be an addition of numerical strength to any political party. UPSOUND ANELE MDA CLIP 0017 @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate I'm not looking to be a kingmaker because I'm saying the throne is empty and I'm gunning for the throne. CLIP 0017 @00:16:59:12 - 00:17:01:12 Masa: So that's first prize presidency? Anele Mda: Absolutely. The first prize is the presidency. VO 18: Mda’s ambition is impressive, but the likelihood of an independent becoming president is extremely small. So, with just one seat available to them, are they a viable option for voters? @ 01:53 Masa : As a first time voter would you consider voting for an independent @ 02:20 Otsile Nkadimeng, So we Vote I would consider voting for an independent should the right kind of independent emerge. I want a leader or representative I can trust. Currently my dilemma with the party system is I have lots of parties to choose from but the people who are running under these parties can I trust them? @ 03:22 Otsile Nkadimeng, So we Vote I recognize the imperfections of SA democracy at this present time. @ 07:40 Otsile Nkadimeng, So we Vote … so it would be a trade off do you choose the party because we trust a few individuals but it comes with a few rotten apples or would you rather go for an independent who you can more directly hire and fire VO 19: Now, for many of the independent candidates, it’s about sparking change in an imperfect system. DAY 2, CARD 3, C0006 @ 03:57 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate … I've sent an appointment —- as a member of the provincial legislature on the 30th of May so the appointment is already set so it's just for me to go honour it. VO 20: So confident is Mogano about his chances, he’s booked his appointment with Parliament just as the counting of votes begins. It’s an impressive level of confidence that belies the uphill battle faced by the independent candidates contesting next week’s elections. Some are bigger names than others and stand a better chance of being in the final Parliamentary mix. VO 21: If they make it, the question then becomes whether their voices will be heard in an increasingly combative National Assembly.” —-----THE END —--- PROMOS Promo 1 VO 1: Short on supporters and resources, independent candidates are the new kids on the ballot paper 00:29:31:15 - 00:30:02:24 Tshepo Mogano, Independent Candidate —Today, I'm telling South Africans there is a new kid on the block called an independent candidate —- CLIP 0017 @ 00:08:49:03 - 00:08:58:23 Anele Mda, Independent Candidate I'm not looking to be a kingmaker because I'm saying the throne is empty and I'm gunning for the throne. VO 6: But could they be a real game changer in the upcoming elections? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Independent candidates are a new addition to South Africa's democracy. What does an independent candidates election campaign look like - is it enough and IF they secure the seat they dream of - will IT be enough to make the level of impact this country needs?
metadata.Summary: Premise: Are the independent candidates a wasted ballot? There are 325 political parties who will be taking part in this year’s elections. But standing outside the confines of a long-held electoral party system are the outliers: 11 independent candidates who are going against the grain -who believe they can make a difference with only one seat. https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/political-parties-independent-candidates-sign-code-conduct Why? Voters are desperate for alternatives and some people online have been pushing the independent candidate option as a viable one - but is it? In order to answer this question, we spoke to several independent candidates to establish how they will go about instituting impactful changes. Repeatedly, all except one - Anele Mda - stated they are limited as they only have one seat. Begging the question, why pursue independent candidacy if one already feels limited and powerless. In addition, as they are all championing varying issues it provides an opportunity to debate some of the key voter concerns.
metadata.Further information: Interviews Anele Mda She was introduced to politics by her father who was a dedicated member of the ANC. A former COPE MP, Anele had her share of controversy during her tenure. For instance, in 2009, she was suspended from COPE for making sexist and racist remarks. She is an extremely head strong and fiery individual who seems very convicted in her beliefs. Her political experience makes her the strongest of the independent candidates. Controversy seems to follow her as her reaction to the absence of independent candidate photographs raied a few eyebrows. However, when one understand the IEC hasn’t even updated its website to reflect the existence of independent candidates - then perhaps one can comprehend the frustrations. Anele’s key focus areas:- Unemployment - she says she will actively challenge the 12 month internship period because companies are compensated for employing interns yet they fail to make meaningful change. She says it should be a 3 year internship as most entry level roles require 3 years experience. I asked if the issue wasn't sufficient employment opportunities for all coupled with limited entrepreneurial pursuits. In addition, given the climate - would a mandatory three year internship not result in locking new graduates out of an already scarce job market. I also highlighted that the government has spent billions of Rands on youth employment programmes, yet unemployment keeps rising. Scrapping the tender system - she says it has only benefitted a few and needs to go Tshepo Mogano Was formerly in the SANDF for eight years, he said he left because the army did not meet up with his expectations as it was being run unprofessionally. He then worked for a PPP specialising in facilities management, where he was a PA to the CEO he says he is very active in his community in Pretoria and established the body corporate at the estate where he purchased property. He managed to buy the property after he left the PPP and went into the tender business. It would be interesting to juxtapose his views on tenders versus Anele’s intention to have the system scrapped. He has championed a number of small projects in his area and intends to replicate these at provincial level. When asked about policy implementation he stated he will learn as he goes along - it seems he hasn't conducted research in order to understand the political climate in which he intends to operate . Again , he repeatedly referenced the fact he would only have one seat as a barrier to impact he had no how-to-strategy regarding the policies he intends to further. For example , he made reference to drug rehabilitation centres but he did not know about the budgets of the status quo rehabilitation centres around the province. He was uncertain when I asked if he would vote with the ANC and if he would ever receive it in exchange for his vote . Tshepo had a particularly terrible interview at Newzroom Afrika last week where he stated he would vote with the ANC and that Panyaza Lesufi is doing a great job as premier. Political Analyst: Otsile Nkadimeng Highly articulate 19 year old who will be voting for the first time this year. Otsile Nkadimeng is the Founder and Executive Director of So We Vote, a Youth Voting Advocacy Group. He is also the lead organiser of Fridays for Future South Africa and the co-founder of the Sundial Movement, a Climate Network that connects high school students to take collective action on Climate Change. Alongside his role as a Climate Activist.
